references.text: Isaac travels to Gerar because of a famine, mirroring Abram's journey to Egypt due to famine.
Abraham goes to Gerar and presents Sarah as his sister, a pattern that repeats from his stay in Egypt.
Jacob sends his sons to Egypt to buy grain during the famine, a parallel to Abram's journey to Egypt because of famine.
God tells Jacob not to be afraid to go down to Egypt, which reflects Abram's journey to Egypt.
The great famine strikes all lands, and people come to Egypt to buy grain—Egypt as a refuge during famine, just as Abram experienced.
Elimelech leaves Bethlehem and goes to Moab because of the famine, a parallel to leaving the promised land during famine.
Stephen speaks about the famine that struck Egypt and Canaan, and how the patriarchs went down to Egypt to get grain.
